$comment: Reviewer pool for /adversarial-review. Ported to web from mlorentedev/dotfiles
(HARNESS-071, dotfiles#955) to close web#277.
EVERY bare issue number in the source file was a dotfiles number. They are
qualified here, and repo-relative paths are marked, because an unqualified
`#955` in this repo resolves to web#955 — a different issue that exists. That
is the collision recorded in dotfiles#1437 and in docs/lessons/lesson-031.
Allow-list of models permitted to SIGN a review.md. Since HARNESS-093 the
launcher DRAWS one member at random; the whole array is the gate's allow-list,
which `dotf spec archive` enforces via checkReviewGate.
Standing rule: an adversarial review never runs on an Anthropic model. The
reviewer must not be the implementer, and Claude implements nearly every
change in this repo.
The incident THIS repo has, and the reason the file landed here: WEB-080's
review (specs/WEB-080/review.md) ran on claude-sonnet-5 against an
implementation by claude-opus-5 — the same family — and nothing declined the
signature, because until now nothing here checked. It was declared in the
review rather than hidden, which is why it was caught at all. In dotfiles the
same class of failure went further: BUG-074 was reviewed twice by
claude-opus-5 before anyone noticed. Declaration is not a mechanism; this file
is.
Entries are model IDS, not tool names, and that distinction is load-bearing:
`agy` also serves claude-opus-4-6-thinking and claude-sonnet-4-6, so pinning
the tool would guarantee nothing. Pinning the id does.
`id` is the canonical string a reviewer records in review.md and the gate
matches on. `provider`/`model` are the launcher's flags, kept explicit rather
than parsed out of `id`: BUG-074 round 3 ran on the right model only because
~/.pi/agent/settings.json on one machine happened to default to it — pi's own
default provider is google, and that file is unversioned per-machine state.
A pin that depends on a default is not a pin.
Every entry declares EXACTLY ONE of `secret_id` or `auth: login`, and the
absence of both is not a safe default — it falls through to an UNSCOPED
`dotf secrets run --`, handing every credential in the registry to a process
that reads none of them, and letting one unrelated broken entry block a
review. Measured in this repo 2026-09-02: an unscoped injection failed on
openrouter-api-key, a credential an adversarial review never touches. Note
that dotfiles guards this with TestEveryPoolEntryDeclaresItsAuth, which reads
dotfiles' OWN file only, via shippedRepoRoot — no test in any repo guards
THIS one, so the declarations below are held by review, not by a check.
Reasoning-class only. The latency-optimised daily models (nan/qwen3.6,
nan/gemma4, the gemini flash tier) are deliberately absent: a reviewer that
PASSes cheaply is worse than no gate, because it converts the gate into a
green checkmark. This file is read once per spec, so slow is fine. The
`-flash` suffix on three members below is NOT that tier — dotfiles'
ai/pi/models.json marks each of them reasoning: true with a 1M context.
Order is provenance, not precedence, since HARNESS-093 (dotfiles#1370): the
launcher draws one member at random, so every entry is exercised in the
ordinary course of reviews and NaN's per-model concurrency buckets are
spread; --reviewer names one deliberately, which is how a run is reproduced.
The roles below record why each member was admitted, not who runs first.
On saturation, measured 2026-08-20: NaN's concurrency limit is PER MODEL, not
per API key (8 concurrent to deepseek gives 5x200 + 3x429, while mimo answers
200 during that saturation). So a spec review launched while the PR reviewer
is saturating deepseek WILL fail, and falling through to another entry is the
correct response rather than a bug. Do not 'fix' that by promoting the NaN
sibling above the provider-diverse entry — it would trade an outage-proof
fallback for a saturation-proof one and lose the stronger property.
Kept in sync with mlorentedev/dotfiles/harness/reviewer-pool.json by hand.
mlorentedev/kubelab's copy is STALE as of 2026-09-02 — it predates the auth
requirement and declares neither field on any of its three entries. Do not
port from there.

pool.why: 1M context and a mandatory reasoning chain — roughly 4x slower than qwen3.6 on trivial prompts, which is the correct trade for a gate that runs once per spec. Exercised: BUG-074 round 3 (in dotfiles) re-ran the mutation battery itself rather than trusting the spec's table.

A second provider family, independent of both NaN and Anthropic — provider diversity rather than merely a different model. Pro tier at high effort; the flash tiers are excluded for the same reason qwen3.6 is. agy has no --provider flag; the model id selects the family. AUTH IS LOGIN, not a key (dotfiles#1156): agy holds an OAuth token at ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/google_credentials.json and answers with no API key in the environment at all (measured 2026-08-22, re-confirmed on this machine 2026-09-02). This entry previously named GEMINI_API_KEY, a secret the registry has never declared, so every attempt to use the provider-diverse arm died at `dotf secrets run --only` — and nothing noticed, because the primary always answered. The arm this pool exists to provide had therefore never run once. It is also the ONLY member that runs while the secrets vault is locked, which makes it the reproducible choice on a machine that has not been unlocked.

Admitted 2026-08-20 after the evaluation this file's bar requires, and the verdict is recorded honestly rather than as a pass. What WAS established: given the same planted-defect shell snippet, mimo returned a real, correct finding. It is reasoning-class by profile (1M context, reasoning chain) against qwen3.6 and gemma4's 262K, which is the line this pool draws. What was NOT established: a quality RANKING against deepseek. deepseek never produced content under the same harness — it spent 29,299 characters of reasoning and returned finish_reason=length with an EMPTY body at 8,000 output tokens, so there was nothing to compare against. That is an instrumentation result, not a capability one, and it is stated here so nobody reads this entry as 'mimo matched deepseek'. It is admitted as a SECOND fallback, after the provider-diverse one, because provider diversity remains the stronger property.
pool.operational_note: Reasoning models here emit reasoning_content BEFORE content. Under-provisioning max_tokens returns an empty body with finish_reason=length and no error — the same shape as a review that silently did not happen. Provision generously and check finish_reason; deepseek did not answer within 8,000 output tokens on a small prompt.

pool.why: Admitted 2026-08-29 by owner decision (HARNESS-093, dotfiles#1370) to spread reviews across NaN's PER-MODEL concurrency buckets and exercise more than one model on the gate. What IS established: reasoning-class by profile — dotfiles' ai/pi/models.json marks glm5.3-flash reasoning: true with a 1M context, the line this pool draws (dotfiles' tests/reviewer-pool.bats holds it). What is NOT established: a calibration against a review of known outcome; recorded here so nobody reads this entry as measured equivalence to deepseek. Drawn at random like every member; --reviewer names it deliberately.
